Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 83, verse 30–36:

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said:

﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾ ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided."﴾ ﴿But they had not been sent as guardians over them.﴾ ﴿So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿Upon couches, looking on.﴾ ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾

The pronoun in "marrū" (they passed by) refers to the believers, though it may also refer to the disbelievers. As for the pronoun in "yataghāmazūn" (they winked at one another), it refers to the disbelievers and cannot refer to anything else. Likewise in His words, "inqalabū" (they returned) and "fākihīn" (jesting): its meaning is those possessing fruit, pleasure, vigor and joy, through their belittling of the believers. It is said: "rajulun fākihun" (a man who is fākih), like "lābin" and "tāmir," and so on, with an alif, and this is the reading of the majority. It is also said: "rajulun fakihun" (a man who is fakih), from this same meaning. Ḥafṣ, on the authority of ʿĀṣim, read "fakihīn" without an alif, and this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima.

As for the pronoun in "ra'aw" (they saw) and "qālū" (they said), al-Ṭabarī and others said it refers to the disbelievers, and the meaning is that they accuse the believers of misguidance, while the disbelievers had not been sent as guardians over the believers. Another group said: rather, the meaning is the reverse, and the meaning of the verse is: when the believers saw the disbelievers, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided," and this is the truth concerning them; but this stirs up speech among them. So there is in the verse an exhortation to peaceful disengagement, i.e., the believers were not sent as guardians over the disbelievers. All of this is abrogated, according to this interpretation, by the verse of the sword.

Since the preceding verses have spoken of the Day of Resurrection, and that woe on that day is for the deniers, it is permissible for Him to say "fa-al-yawm" (so today) in narration of what will be said and will occur on that day. And "alladhīna" (those who) is in the nominative as the subject of a nominal sentence. His words, ﴿upon couches, looking on﴾, mean: at their enemies in the Fire. Kaʿb said: "For the people of Paradise there are windows through which they look out." Others said: "Between them is a great transparent body, through which they see their condition."

"Hal thuwwiba" (Have they been rewarded?) is a confirmation and a questioning addressed to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community. It may be intended as: "they look, [asking] whether it has been rewarded," so the looking falls upon "hal thuwwiba," and the meaning is: has it been recompensed? It may also be that the meaning is: some of them say to others. Ibn Muḥaysin, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read "hatthuwwiba" with the assimilation of the lām into the thāʾ, because they are close in place of articulation. The rest read "hal thuwwiba" without assimilation. In His words "mā kānū" (what they used to do) there is an ellipsis, its estimated meaning being: the recompense of what they used to do, or the punishment of what they used to do.

The commentary of Surah [al-Muṭaffifīn] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
